correctness.rationale: For each degree d>=1, exact 2d-root DFT orthogonality isolates all non-Nyquist squared-intensity Fourier coefficients. The two top-harmonic observations invert a 2x2 real matrix of determinant -sin(d Delta). Equality of two full concentric-circle moduli forces a rational quotient invariant under a real dilation factor different from one, hence constant. Explicit degree-one and degree-d pairs prove respectively the equal-radius and resonant-angle necessity. Zero polynomial and vanishing endpoint coefficients are accounted for. The included 6048-assertion deterministic checker verifies identity calculations for d=1 through d=12; the all-degree theorem is proved algebraically, not numerically.

originality.rationale: The specific new all-degree result is an iff classification of balanced equal-cardinality regular 2d-gon intensities on two concentric circles. The identical 4d count and whole-circle rigidity were known. Pohl–Li–Boche use 2d+1 plus 2d-1 concentric sites, Bodmann–Hammen use intersecting circles, Grohs–Liehr–Rathmair address an infinite-dimensional Fock setting, and a previously established degree-two balanced case is acknowledged, not reclaimed. Full relevant earlier statements were compared; priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: A separately published degree-two version is covered; only the uniform all-degree balanced-grid classification is asserted.

value.rationale: Balances the established natural 4d sampling budget across two identical FFT-sized polygonal orbits, and gives an exact necessary-and-sufficient phase-offset design criterion for every degree. This resolves the practical structural question left unanswered by the earlier unbalanced 2d+1 versus 2d-1 concentric design: equal-angular sensor allocation can destroy universality at discrete resonances, no matter how different the radii, but one nonresonant rotation restores it. Explicit global counterexamples and the determinant identifying the sole alias ambiguity make the classification mathematically interpretable; the result is not asserted to improve the known cardinality budget.
